comments.text: A Call to Peace By the Artist for Syria: Syria needs peace in the shade of redemption. Syria needs peace for the burgeoning of a cultural reset. Find your bearing and include rights in your practice. The children will leap from the stalls and prosper. Syria needs peace. Rise up and meet the light, all ye of that nation. Your deliverance is at hand. Combat boots aside, let violence not deride you. Wash yourselves so that you may be cleansed. Wisdom pursue your families. Liberate the nation. Only the chance to find joy once again, Syria. The flowers blossom from the desert, Syria. Rally to find the reception of peace, not the deception of it. Will the power of the mighty knock down the mightier? Should you cast judgement or the first stone? An oasis of peace, let serenity flow there. Palestine is a brother of mine. Israel my sister. Syria my father. Love is the divine ordinance yet lush sects of doves with soft wings fly, can you see them to counter the bombers, olive branches in their mouths? Syria, wash like a wave of smooth balm, a nectar reside for once again, bringing sweet honey to the wayfarers in the desert. Honey, not blood, will ravage the rocks. Syria, meet yourself in the reflection of peace. Let me meet you in a handshake of agreement...solve the plan that aims toward Iran: meet it with peace. Jordan, Lebanon, Egypt, Iraq, and Cyprus. See the cloves of Yemen, the ancillary sands of Saudi Arabia, the dancing in the night, arms clasped together. "Find in the spaces a lion to be tamed," she says, Miriam of the Nile reeds, true princess of peace and the land's only directorial author for good. Bethsheba in all her glory found not the story told by her, a maternal sway that she seduced the world to; changed the world was after, replacing guns with laughter. Peace, O Syria, is your nation's gift. Directed by Daniel Kubishta
